body:
I'll start by examining the root files and directory structure, then plan the capture.

Let me copy the roots verbatim and inspect the wiki index structure.

Let me extract all links from the wiki index to discover the category tree.

I have the link tree. Let me check network access, verify URL base, and check the python.org doc index for old moin links.

Network works; URL base confirmed. Let me fetch all 13 category index pages and record statuses.

All 13 fetched successfully. Now let me enumerate leaf links within each category index.

I have the full category tree. Let me fetch ~40 high-relevance leaf pages (55 files total).

All fetches returned 200. Let me verify content quality and probe old moin URLs for the authority/URL note.

Key finding: pages carry an explicit MoinMoin migration disclaimer. Let me inspect content bodies and the doc-index link contexts.

Rich evidence found. Let me extract substantive body text with line numbers from high-value pages.

Let me extract bodies from the remaining high-value categories.

Let me capture structural line cites from the wiki index and doc index.

Now let me generate precise manifest data (bytes, lines, URLs) for every captured file.

Let me confirm every planned citation with `rg -n` before writing the manifest.

Let me verify the complete category tree names from the index before writing.

Now I'll write the complete MANIFEST.md with all rows, facts, and caveats.

Let me verify the manifest's aggregate claims and row counts.

I need to correct one aggregate number in the manifest.

Let me validate every `file:LINE` citation in the manifest resolves to a real line.

Assignment complete. `/tmp/python-research/wiki/MANIFEST.md` (22,460 B, 216 lines) contains the 59-file table (`file | exact URL | bytes | lines | why critical`), 40 `rg -n`-verified line-cited facts, the category tree, and caveats. All 43 unique citation refs were validated against real lines; both root copies are `cmp`-identical to their sources. The ai-guides repo was not touched.

**Capture:** 2 verbatim root copies + 13 category indexes + 44 leaf pages = 59 files, 1,692,572 bytes. All 57 wiki fetches returned HTTP 200 — **no 404s, no `MISSING` files, nothing fabricated**. Hidden audit logs `.fetch-status` and `.leaf-list` record every URL/status.

**Authority / URL note (honest):** The wiki is community-curated and lower-authority than `docs.python.org/3`. `wiki-index.html:216` carries the MoinMoin migration warning ("information may be outdated"); the same disclaimer appears in 45 captured files, and `guides__index.html:239`, `getting-started__index.html:233`, `security__index.html:221` explicitly warn about legacy/thin community content. The new Sphinx site uses `https://wiki.python.org/python/...` (`wiki-index.html:157` → `psf/wiki/blob/main/python/index.md`), while python.org/doc still links old `https://wiki.python.org/moin/...` URLs (`:288`, `:322`, `:408`, `:472`, `:473`, `:544`, `:665`, `:697`, `:777`) alongside one new-style link (`:280`, `:463`, `:657`). Probed moin URLs are still live (200) but legacy.

**Category tree discovered** (29 top-level sections from `wiki-index.html:82-108`, `310-360`): Archive; Books & Publications; Community & User Groups; Conferences; Database Programming*; Documentation*; Editors & IDEs; Education; Getting Started*; GUI Programming; Guides and How-Tos*; Internationalization; Python Implementations*; Infrastructure; Language Reference*; Libraries & Tools*; Multimedia & Games; Networking; Packaging*; Performance*; Platform-Specific; Python Software Foundation (skipped); Python 3 Migration*; Scientific Computing; Security*; Summer of Code (skipped); Sprints (skipped); Testing*; Web Development*. Sibling wikis: PSF Wiki, Jython Wiki. `* = target category captured; PSF/events/jobs skipped.`

**8 high-value wiki facts (line-cited):**
- `language__Generators.html:263` — generators are iterator-like functions usable in a `for` loop.
- `language__Generators.html:266` — code simplification is an explicit benefit of generators/generator expressions.
- `performance__PythonSpeed.html:259` — set/dict membership O(1) vs sequence O(n).
- `performance__PythonSpeed.html:264` — `collections.deque` gives O(1) queues vs O(n) list rebuilds.
- `guides__HandlingExceptions.html:283` — catch specific exceptions; a catch-all can misreport `KeyboardInterrupt`.
- `testing__UnitTests.html:237` — doctest embeds tests in docstrings (executable documentation).
- `py3__Python2orPython3.html:255` — Python 3 for new work; Python 2 EOL with no security fixes.
- `security__index.html:221` — wiki security coverage is thin; PSRT/current docs are the better source.
